result.title: Ref2Light: From One Image to Interactive Glasses-Free 3D Characters
result.summary: Animating character illustrations on light-field displays demands coherent binocular parallax, real-time pose articulation, and fine-grained expression control. However, existing 2D animation and 3D reconstruction pipelines cannot combine these with rapid character switching. We present Ref2Light, a feed-forward framework that maps a single A-pose illustration and continuous pose and expression controls to display-native light-field animation, without per-character 3D reconstruction, rigging, or test-time optimization. Our key insight is to decompose light-field synthesis into static identity, view-dependent parallax, and control-driven articulation. A shared encoder caches multi-scale identity features once per character for rapid switching. A conditional decoder then synthesizes ordered angular anchors from these features via backward texture transport and direct color synthesis. A global-local control scheme deforms the anchors with head-body controls and uses the updated correspondence fields to track facial regions across views for masked local facial refinement. Finally, calibrated differentiable subpixel interlacing converts the anchors into the native panel raster, enabling end-to-end native supervision without rendering all views at full resolution. On held-out VRoid identities, Ref2Light reduces head-body LPIPS by 20.1%-55.6% over 2D and 3D baselines and lowers non-target change MAE in mouth closure by 95.6%-96.5% versus monolithic decoding, while running at 34.0-40.1 FPS for 1440x2560 native rasters on a consumer GPU. Code and demo are in the Supplementary Material.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Ref2Light，用单张 A-pose 插画直接前馈生成光场显示器上的 3D 角色动画，通过分解身份、视角视差与控制驱动形变并配合缓存身份特征实现快速切换。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于图像到 3D 显示内容的生成与渲染工程，虽有多尺度特征缓存和对应场局部细化，但服务于视差合成而非推理状态、证据使用或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的实质联系。
